title: AIchain User Truth (Layer 3)
description: Passive local configuration describing everything the user already has and wants. Never leaves the machine. Consumed by aichaind together with the global catalog_manifest.json to compute effective cost and pick providers.

profile.description: Active routing preference. Presets map to weight overrides over the catalog role weights.

mode.description: economy = free paths first, paid only as last resort; power = best role_score regardless of cost within budget; custom = use weights below.

custom_weights.description: Only read when mode=custom. Must sum to 1.0.

min_intelligence.description: Hard floor: never route to a model below this normalized intelligence score, even in economy mode.

budget.description: Spending ceilings. aichaind tracks actual token spend against these and degrades to cheaper/free paths as ceilings approach.

soft_threshold.description: Fraction of the limit at which the router starts preferring free paths regardless of mode.

hard_stop.description: If true, paid providers are refused once a limit is hit; only free and local paths remain.

assets.description: What the user already owns. These change effective cost: a flat-rate subscription makes marginal cost ~0 up to its fair-use ceiling.

access_type.description: app_only subscriptions are informational: aichaind will surface them as a suggestion ('this task fits your Pro plan — open the app') but never bridges them programmatically.

api_keys.description: Providers with a configured key. Keys themselves live in the OS keyring / env, NOT in this file — this only declares existence and metadata.

key_ref.description: Name of env var or keyring entry holding the key.

free_quotas.description: Free tiers the user has activated. aichaind decrements usage locally and resets on the stated cadence.

local_models.description: Locally hosted open-weight models. Effective cost 0; speed measured by aichaind probes.

catalog_ref.description: Optional link to the catalog entry so global intelligence scores apply.

privacy.description: Data-boundary rules. Evaluated BEFORE any scoring — a request that matches a rule is constrained to the allowed destinations no matter what scores say.

match.description: Simple matchers; at least one must be present.

tags.description: User- or harness-supplied request tags, e.g. 'work', 'personal', 'sensitive'.

max_fallback_depth.description: How many chain links to try before returning an error.

sticky_session.description: Prefer keeping one conversation on one model unless it fails.
